fixes.title: Remove duplicate relationships
fixes.description: The same predecessor/successor pair linked more than once with the same type.
fixes.effect: Deletes the extra TASKPRED rows, keeping the first of each.

fixes.title: Remove self-referencing logic
fixes.description: Relationships where an activity is its own predecessor.

fixes.title: Correct out-of-sequence logic
fixes.description: Links the recorded progress has broken - a successor that started before its predecessor finished, or finished before it did.
fixes.effect: Replaces each broken FS link with the parts of it the actual dates still satisfy: SS where the successor started after the predecessor started, FF where it can still finish (or did finish) after it. An FS implies both, so this only relaxes the planner's logic - it never adds a dependency nobody drew, and never one the recorded dates contradict. Links already present are not duplicated. Broken SS and FF links have nothing weaker to fall back to, so they are left for a planner, as is an FS the dates contradict entirely. Links still holding back open work change the forecast when P6 reschedules; recorded-history links are proved to move no date. Each converted link swaps an FS for SS and/or FF, which lowers the Finish-to-Start share in health check 4.

choices.label: Only those still holding back open work (P6's out-of-sequence list)
Also links broken by work that has since finished (as-built record)

fixes.title: Tie in dangling activity ends
fixes.description: Open activities whose finish drives nothing (only SS successors) or whose start nothing drives (only FF/SF predecessors), although they have logic.
fixes.effect: Adds the partner link beside the one already there - FF to each open SS successor, SS from each FF predecessor - so both ends sit in the network. Successors that have already finished are left alone, since an FF would contradict their dates. Dates can move: that is the float the open end was hiding.

fixes.title: Remove redundant relationships
fixes.description: FS links a longer FS path already implies (A → C where A → B → C exists).
fixes.effect: Deletes only links that are provably implied on work not yet started - then reschedules to prove no date or float moves, and keeps any that would. Links the proof cannot cover stay in the Insights list.

fixes.description: Leads pull a successor forward and hide float; many specifications ban them.
fixes.effect: Rewrites lag_hr_cnt. Dates will move when P6 reschedules.

coverage.name: Lags
coverage.why: A long lag usually stands for real work - curing, delivery, approval. Replace it with an activity in P6, or shorten it if the gap is not real.

coverage.name: Relationship types
coverage.why: The mix of relationship types describes how the work overlaps. There is no correct automatic conversion of SS or FF to FS - it would change the plan, not tidy it.

coverage.name: High float
coverage.why: High float is almost always missing successor logic. Add the successor the work actually enables.

coverage.name: Negative float
coverage.why: Negative float is the programme reporting that it cannot meet a date. It is removed by recovering time (re-sequencing, resourcing) or by an agreed later date - editing the data would only hide it.

coverage.name: High duration
coverage.why: Split long activities into the pieces that are planned and progressed separately.

coverage.name: Invalid dates
coverage.why: Forecast dates before the data date are cleared by rescheduling in P6 (F9). Actual dates after the data date need the real date entered.

coverage.name: Resources / cost loading
coverage.why: Resources and costs have to come from the estimate - they cannot be invented from the programme.

coverage.name: Missed activities
coverage.why: This measures delivery against plan. It records what happened; it is not a data error.

coverage.name: Baseline Execution Index (BEI)
coverage.why: BEI measures delivery against the baseline. It records performance; it is not a data error.

coverage.name: High float caused by missing successors
coverage.why: Add the successor the work actually enables.

coverage.name: Remaining work with no resources or cost
coverage.why: Resources and costs have to come from the estimate.

coverage.name: Work recorded out of sequence
coverage.why: These no longer move any date, so the repair leaves them alone by default. To correct them too, choose “Also links broken by work that has since finished” in the out-of-sequence card.
